ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=x^2+bx+c$ passes through point $A(-4,0)$ and point $C(0,-4)$, with another intersection point with the x-axis being B. What is the analytical expression of this parabola?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since the parabola $y={x}^{2}+bx+c$ passes through points $A\left(-4,0\right)$ and $C\left(0,-4\right)$,\\
thus $\begin{cases}16-4b+c=0\\ c=-4\end{cases}$,\\
therefore $\begin{cases}b=3\\ c=-4\end{cases}$,\\
hence the equation of the parabola is $\boxed{y={x}^{2}+3x-4}$;
